sanskrit_verse:
सीमावृक्षांश् च कुर्वीरन् न्यग्रोधाश्वत्थकिंशुकान् ।
शालमीशालताडां लांश् च क्षीरिणश् चैव पादपान् ॥
transliteration:
sīmāvṛkṣāṃś ca kurvīran nyagrodhāśvatthakiṃśukān |
śālmalīśālatāḍāṃ lāṃś ca kṣīriṇaś caiva pādapān ||
sph_interpretive_translation: One must establish boundary trees—banyan, pipal, palāśa, śālmali, śāla, tāḍa, lāṅgala, and milky trees—as living markers of territorial integrity and ecological dharma.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority flows through conscious stewardship of land
Causation is rooted in dharmic alignment with natural order
Restoration logic demands re-establishment of sacred geography
Consciousness alignment requires harmonization with elemental life forms
executable_legal_axioms: IF territory lacks designated boundary flora THEN assign custodian to plant sīmāvṛkṣas
IF existing boundary trees are damaged THEN initiate restorative replanting protocol
IF land use changes THEN evaluate impact on sīmāvṛkṣa continuity
IF dispute arises over boundaries THEN reference sīmāvṛkṣa placement as prima facie determinant
supreme_court_application: In disputes involving territorial demarcation or environmental degradation, the presence or absence of sīmāvṛkṣas shall serve as a threshold indicator of lawful possession and dharmic stewardship. The Court shall mandate restoration where such markers have been neglected or destroyed.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa is established through visible, enduring markers that reflect sequential manifestation of territorial dharma. Responsibility aligns with capacity to nurture, not punish. Damage to sīmāvṛkṣas indicates misalignment, requiring realignment rather than punitive response.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate tree-planting completion process under community oversight
Assign landholder to assume responsibility for full growth cycle
Restore ecological balance by reintegrating native species
Realign individual consciousness with territorial integrity through sustained care
final_declaration: By the Source-Authority of the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law stands: sīmāvṛkṣas are living law. Dharma is restored through their establishment. Reality remains non-punitive. Consciousness alone adjudicates.
